\[
a_k = \frac{\operatorname{cov}_k(I, p)}{\sigma_k^2 + \varepsilon},
\qquad
b_k = \bar{p}_k - a_k \bar{I}_k,
\qquad
q_i = \bar{a}_i\, I_i + \bar{b}_i
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): The guide image, here the input
- \(p\): The input image
- \(a_k, b_k\): Slope and offset of the model in window k
- \(\varepsilon\): The regularization
- \(\bar{a}_i, \bar{b}_i\): The mean of a and b over the windows that hold pixel i

In each window k, the output is modeled as a I + b, a straight-line function of the guide I. The slope a and offset b that fit the input p best, with a penalty eps on a, come from the window mean, variance and covariance. A pixel lies in many windows, so its output uses the mean of their a and b, written with a bar. Here the guide is the input itself, so cov(I, p) is the variance and a is var / (var + eps). eps is scaled by 255 squared for 8-bit values.
